title: Concurrency + edge-removal + agent-control are foundational (proven by a live collision)
summary: On 2026-06-08 a human re-plan in one session silently RACED a live autonomous agent (sub-planner) in another, on the same task graph. The system had no defense: both wrote status, last-write-won (the agent overrode a human cancel until it finished), and there was no way to SEE or STOP the other worker except grepping ps. This exposed 3 foundational gaps that MUST be fixed before 'graph-coordinated parallelism + self-improvement' (the product's moat) is safe: (1) no edge removal -> can't re-parallelize a graph; (2) no concurrency-safe status -> cancels/edits race, last-write-wins; (3) no cross-session agent visibility/control -> can't see or cooperatively stop a colliding worker. Also note: not all work parallelizes — these 3 fixes edit the SAME core files (daemon.js/overlay.js/mcp-core.js), so they must be done SERIALLY; shared mutable files are a true serializer (worktree isolation doesn't apply since the code lives outside the cwd workspace).
